title: December, 2020
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies · the aggregator
logline: Does Chloe come home. The last December of the public strip. Not this year. The mailbox, the phone, the garage. Three days before the end.

panels.composition: The mailbox. Empty. WOOD and BARNABY II. Rain.

image.prompt: a man opening an empty roadside mailbox in December rain, a three-legged dog, clean ink with a slate wash

panels.composition: The flip phone. No text. 4:10 on its screen — the bus's time, still, in his head.

image.prompt: close-up of an old flip phone showing no messages and the time 4:10

panels.composition: The garage. Wood at the table. The last week's strips on the board, six ordinary dailies. Tomorrow's Sunday, blank, taped down.

image.prompt: a man at a drafting table with six finished daily strips pinned above it and a blank Sunday sheet taped to the board

panels.composition: The garage from the door. The lamp. The man. The dog. The blank sheet. Christmas Eve. She does not come home. The strip has three days left and looks like every other night.

image.prompt: a garage studio from its doorway on a rainy night with a man at a lit drafting table before a blank sheet, a dog in a bed beneath, no words

art.line: razor-sharp brush and ink; Sundays wet-on-wet
art.palette: ink and one tone; Sundays gray-green, fog, rust

notes: The last December fixture. She does not come home. The Sunday sheet is blank on the board.
